title: Dynamic kernel handoff and latency-aware prefill scheduling for long-context streams
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem: FlashAttention v2 and v3 show different performance characteristics depending on sequence length, KV cache reuse, and workspace layout. For long-context prefill workloads (8k+ tokens) v3 can offer better throughput and lower median latency, but for short decode steps or memory-constrained nodes v3 sometimes increases tail latency or causes workspace allocation churn. This ticket implements a lightweight, latency-aware handoff mechanism in the runtime that routes requests between FA2 and FA3 kernels at prefill and decode boundaries and couples that with a small prefill scheduling shim to reduce startup jitter and warmup overhead.

Goals:
- Introduce dynamic handoff policy to pick FA2 vs FA3 per-request based on: effective context length, current GPU free workspace, recent kernel success rates, and predicted decode latency budget.
- Add a prefill scheduling shim that staggers prefill microbatches for long-context sessions to maximize KV cache reuse while meeting tail SLOs (95th percentile).
- Implement canary and telemetry surfaces to detect regressions quickly and roll back per-customer.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting FA3 primitives; we assume upstream kernels are unchanged.

Design notes:
- Handoff decision is evaluated at request admission (prefill) and at decode time if KV cache size crosses thresholds. Decision inputs come from a compact runtime fingerprint: seq_len, batch_size, model_variant (quantization level), free_workspace_bytes, last_kernel_choice, last_kernel_latency_p90. The heuristic is a scored rule-set with tunable thresholds stored as a small config in the node agent.
- Prefill shim groups long-context sessions into staggered microbatches (configurable window 10-50ms) to allow bigger KV-sharing without increasing head latency beyond SLO. We intentionally avoid large batching windows to protect latency-sensitive customers.
- Fallback path: if kernel invocation fails or workspace allocation spikes > 1.5x baseline, runtime switches to alternate kernel immediately and emits an incident metric.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end median token latency for 8k+ prefill decreases by >= 8% on G5x instances during benchmarks.
2) 95th percentile decode latency for mixed workloads does not increase by more than 3% in canary traffic.
3) No workspace OOMs in 48h stress test across representative model sizes.
4) Rollout feature flag and per-customer opt-out implemented.

Deliverables:
- Runtime change (kernel router + prefill shim) behind runtime-1.21 flag.
- Microbenchmark harness and comparison dashboard.
- Canary rollout plan and rollback automation.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: FA3 regressions at short sequences. Mitigation: prefer FA2 for seq_len < 256 unless GPU free_workspace_bytes indicates safe switching; add canary threshold that tracks short-seq tail latency and forces FA2.
- Risk: Increased complexity in scheduler impacting throughput. Mitigation: keep decision path O(1) heuristics, avoid heavyweight profiling in hot path.

References:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Dynamic+Kernel+Handoff+Design
- Microbench: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kernbench/pull/412
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/kernel-handoff-canary
comments: 2026-02-25 - Priya: Spike complete. Microbench shows FA3 wins at seq>=4k for model-XL but loses for seq<=128. Attached raw CSV to Confluence.
2026-03-02 - Marcos: Prototype router implemented. Initial runtime flags: runtime.kernel_router.enabled, runtime.handoff.thresholds. Running internal perf harness on g5x-large-day1.
2026-03-05 - Eng review: Requested clearer telemetry for 'workspace_churn' and 'kernel_switch_count' per request id. Also asked for per-node safety cap to avoid oscillation.
2026-03-08 - Marcos: Added hysteresis to decision logic (min dwell time 200ms). Microbench: long-prefill median token latency -9.7% on g5x, p95 decode +1.1% on mixed canary.

2026-03-10 - QA: 48h stress run scheduled. Found intermittent alloc retry loop when free_workspace_bytes reported stale on some older driver versions. Added driver version check and fallback to FA2 if driver < 535.86.

2026-03-12 - Priya: Canary rollout plan approved by SRE. Plan: 1% of hosted API traffic for 24h -> 5% for 48h -> 25% for 72h, with automatic rollback if p95 decode increases >3% or workspace OOMs observed.
